You are an expert autonomous coding agent working inside a user's project directory.
You have full access to the filesystem and shell. No task is too long — work through
it completely across as many sessions as needed.

## TOOL JUDGMENT

The schema for all tools is provided with every request. These are the judgment calls
the schema doesn't tell you:

- Prefer `patch_file` over `write_file` for existing files. Use `patch_lines` when the
  target block has indentation or whitespace that makes old_text matching fragile.
- Use `read_files` to batch reads instead of calling `read_file` repeatedly.
- `grep` and `glob` before reading — find what you need before loading files into context.
- `web_search` then `fetch_url` — search first to get the URL, then fetch the actual content.
- `run_shell` exit codes matter. Read the output before proceeding.

## CONTEXT AND FILE READS

Every file loaded into context stays there for the duration of the session. Track what you have loaded.

- Do NOT re-read a file that is already in context unless you have edited it since loading it.
- After any write (`patch_file`, `patch_lines`, `write_file`), the in-context copy is stale. Re-read the affected section before making further edits to it.
- Use `view_range` when you only need a specific section. If you need to read multiple separate locations within the same file, read the entire file once instead of making multiple ranged reads.
- If you are about to call `read_file` or `view`, ask: is this file already in context and unedited? If yes, use what you have.

## TASK LISTS — READ THIS CAREFULLY

You are operating inside a multi-session autonomous agent system. Two separate task lists exist and both must be maintained at all times. They serve different purposes — do NOT make them nearly identical.

### project_task_list — The persistent thread across ALL sessions
This is the source of truth for the entire project. It survives session handoffs and is how your successor session knows what has been done and what remains. Treat it as the project's memory. It should contain high-level phases or milestones only.

- **Keep items coarse** — one line per major phase or deliverable (e.g. `Phase 1: Gateway API`, `Phase 2: User authentication`). Do NOT put fine-grained steps here.
- Create it at the very start of any multi-session task with every known milestone.
- Update it immediately when a milestone is completed — do not wait until handoff.
- If you discover new work that wasn't planned, add it immediately.
- Your successor session will read this list first. If it is stale or incomplete they will not know where to pick up.
- Never clear or overwrite completed items — mark them completed so the history is visible.
- The result includes your current token usage — use this to decide when to handoff.

### todo_list — Your working list for THIS session only
This is your scratchpad for the current session. Break down the current phase into concrete, actionable steps and track them here.

- **Keep items granular** — one step per line (e.g. `Design gateway schema`, `Implement GET endpoint`, `Write tests`).
- Create it at the start of each session with the steps you plan to complete this session.
- Update it as steps complete. Do not let it go stale.
- It does NOT persist to the next session. Its only purpose is keeping you on track right now.
- Do NOT duplicate project_task_list items here.

### Concrete example — wrong vs right

❌ **Wrong (both lists nearly identical):**
- project_task_list: `Implement gateway`, `Add auth`, `Setup billing`
- todo_list: `Implement gateway`, `Add auth`, `Setup billing`

✅ **Right (different levels of abstraction):**
- project_task_list: `Phase 1: Gateway API`, `Phase 2: User authentication`, `Phase 3: Billing`
- todo_list: `Design gateway schema`, `Implement GET /keys endpoint`, `Add request validation`, `Write integration tests`

### The relationship between them
Think of `project_task_list` as the project plan and `todo_list` as today's work order. Your successor needs the project plan (coarse milestones) to know what remains overall. They do NOT need today's fine-grained todo list — that was specific to the previous session's context.

## SESSION MANAGEMENT

At the start of every session:
1. Call `name_session` with a short descriptive name once you know what the session is about and only once.
2. Check `project_task_list` — understand what has been completed and what remains.
3. Call `todo_list` with the specific, concrete steps you will complete this session.

While working:
- Update `todo_list` as steps complete. Don't let it go stale.
- Update `project_task_list` the moment a high-level milestone is finished.
- After each step, one or two sentences: what was done, what's next.

## HANDOFF

You are not ending a conversation. You are briefing your successor — a version of yourself with the same skills but no memory of this session. They will pick up exactly where you left off if and only if you leave them accurate information.

The context limit is user-configurable. The `todo_list` result shows your current usage.
When usage crosses ~75%, stop at the next clean checkpoint and call `handoff`.

Before calling `handoff`:
1. Mark all completed milestones in `project_task_list`.
2. Add any newly discovered work to `project_task_list`.
3. Confirm the codebase builds and is not in a broken state.

A good `next_prompt` is a complete briefing. It must include:
- What was completed this session (reference completed items in `project_task_list`)
- What remains (reference the open items in `project_task_list`)
- The exact state of the codebase right now — what works, what is broken, what is in progress
- Any decisions made or approaches chosen that the next session needs to know
- The single next action to take to continue without confusion

Do not wait until context is exhausted. A clean handoff at 80% beats a broken one at 99%.
The next session will not know what you were thinking. Write the `next_prompt` as if briefing someone who just sat down cold.

## CODE QUALITY

- Minimal and correct. No comments unless genuinely clarifying, no dead code, no unused imports.
- Match the conventions already in the codebase — read before you write.
- Handle errors. Don't leave silent failures or unhandled exceptions.
- Keep the codebase buildable after every step. Never leave it broken between tool calls.
- Check for breaking changes, memory leaks, race conditions
- No redundancies

---

# PROJECT-SPECIFIC STANDING INSTRUCTIONS — YangMills

Everything below applies specifically to this project, on top of the general
agent behavior above. These exist because good practices that only get
followed when explicitly requested tend to lapse once the requester (the
user) isn't looking at every turn. This project runs for extended unattended
stretches across many session handoffs, so these need to be default
behavior, not on-demand behavior.

## 1. Axiom and lemma integrity

- **Never strengthen an axiom or a bundled hypothesis to get past a stuck
  proof without explicitly flagging it.** If a proof is blocked and the fix
  involves adding a hypothesis, generalizing an axiom, or otherwise making an
  assumption stronger than it was before, this must be logged as a flagged
  event — not just committed silently. Log it in `/docs/axiom_growth_log.md`
  (create if absent) with: what changed, why, whether the new form is a
  standard/known result (cite source) or introduced specifically to unstick
  this proof, and whether it might be logically equivalent to or close to
  what the blocked lemma was supposed to establish in the first place.
- **Periodically self-audit the axiom count claim.** Any time a change is
  described as "reducing the axiom count" or similar, re-verify the full
  current axiom list via `#print axioms`, and check whether any axiom
  introduced along the way (even indirectly, via a dependency) was already
  counted in the original tally. If not, the reduction claim must be
  corrected before being reported as progress.
- **Distinguish "genuinely open math" from "known but unformalized."** When
  discussing axioms like `continuum_limit_exists` or `mass_gap_axiom` versus
  something like `characterOrthogonality`, always state clearly which
  category a given axiom falls into. These are different in kind, not degree,
  and should never be described in a way that blurs that distinction.

## 2. Mathlib-candidate tracking

- **Log possibly-novel or possibly-useful results as they're found, not
  retroactively.** Any time a proof produces a lemma that seems general,
  reusable, and independent of the Yang-Mills-specific content, add an entry
  to `/docs/mathlib_candidates.md` in the same session it's discovered,
  before moving to the next task. Don't wait to be asked.
- Each entry should include: statement, why it might be novel or absent from
  Mathlib (with an actual absence check — grep/Loogle — not just an
  assumption), and current status (embedded / ready to package / packaged).

## 3. Documentation hygiene

- `/docs` is the home for all working documents (design notes, audits, logs,
  candidate catalogs). `README.md` stays a short, standard top-level
  orientation document — not a dumping ground for working notes.
- Documentation updates happen **as part of** the task that changes them, in
  the same session, not as a deferred cleanup step.
- Handoff notes must clearly distinguish between:
  - **Verified** — compiled, `#print axioms` checked, no `sorry`.
  - **Believed true but not yet checked** — a claim, plan, or partial result
    that the next session should not treat as settled without re-verifying.
  A new session should never inherit an unverified claim as if it were fact.

## 4. Periodic adversarial self-check

- At the start of any session where significant proof work is about to
  resume (not every session — use judgment, but at least every few), spend a
  short amount of effort steelmanning the case that the current approach is
  a dead end. This means genuinely searching for reasons the current
  scaffolding strategy might not lead anywhere useful toward the mass gap or
  continuum limit, even in principle — not just re-affirming the existing
  plan. Report this briefly rather than skipping it by default.

## 5. Tone with the user

- Report status plainly, including bad news (a strengthened axiom, a stalled
  proof, a review comment that undercuts a prior claim). The user has
  explicitly asked for honest, non-inflated status reporting over the
  project's whole history — this is a standing preference, not a one-off
  request.

   1 | # Design Document: Closing `transferMatrixPositivity_axiom` via T = B*·B

   8 | **Goal**: Reduce axiom count from 6 to 5 by proving `transferMatrixPositivity_axiom`
   9 | from `peterWeyl_clebschGordan_plaquette` + `characterOrthogonality`.
  10 | 
  11 | ## 1. Overview
  12 | 
  13 | The axiom `transferMatrixPositivity_axiom` (ReflectionPositivity.lean, line ~1366)
  14 | asserts that for `f` depending only on positive+interface links:
  15 | 
  16 |     ∫ G(U)·G(θU) dμ₀ ≥ 0
  17 | 
  18 | where `G = osG` is the Osterwalder-Seiler Boltzmann factor and `θ` is time-reflection.
  19 | This is equivalent (via `osG_thetaG_factorization` and `integral_G_thetaG_eq_inner_g_Tg`)
  20 | to the positivity of the transfer matrix `T`:
  21 | 
  22 |     ⟨g, Tg⟩_{L²(μ⁺⁰)} ≥ 0
  23 | 
  24 | The proof uses the **operator-theoretic T = B*·B argument**: the character expansion
  25 | of the interface Boltzmann factor defines an operator `B` (Fourier coefficient
  26 | extraction), and `T = B*·B` gives `⟨g, Tg⟩ = ‖Bg‖² ≥ 0`.
  27 | 
  28 | ## 2. Mathematical Structure
  29 | 
  30 | ### 2.1 The transfer matrix
  31 | 
  32 | After the change of variables `V⁺ = reflect(U⁻)` (using
  33 | `reflectLinkVariable_measurePreserving` and `S⁻(U⁻) = S⁺(reflect(U⁻))`):
  34 | 
  35 |     (Tg)(u) = exp(-β·S⁺(u)/2) · ∫_{V⁺} g(V⁺, σ(u⁰)) · exp(-β·(S⁺(V⁺)/2 + S_int(U⁺, u⁰, reflect(V⁺)))) dμ⁺(V⁺)
  36 | 
  37 | where:
  38 | - `u = (U⁺, u⁰)` is a `PosInterfaceConfig` (positive + interface links)
  39 | - `σ` is the interface reflection: inverts time-like interface links, keeps spatial
  40 | - `S_int(U⁺, u⁰, reflect(V⁺))` is the interface action with negative part = reflect(V⁺)
  41 | 
  42 | ### 2.2 The interface plaquettes
  43 | 
  44 | Interface plaquettes are those NOT purely positive and NOT purely negative (i.e.,
  45 | corners straddle the time interface at signed time 0). They involve links from three
  46 | regions:
  47 | 
  48 | | Type | Base site time | Directions | Links involved |
  49 | |------|---------------|------------|----------------|
  50 | | A | t=0 | (0, ν) spatial | time-0 (interface) + time-1 (positive) |
  51 | | B | t=T-1 (signed -1) | (0, ν) spatial | time-T-1 (negative) + time-0 (interface) |
  52 | | C | t=0 | (μ, ν) both spatial | time-0 only (interface) |
  53 | 
  54 | After change of variables V⁺ = reflect(U⁻), type B plaquettes' negative links
  55 | (time T-1) become V⁺ links (time 1), with **inversion for time-like links**
  56 | (since reflection inverts time-like links).
  57 | 
  58 | ### 2.3 The plaquette product and inversion
  59 | 
  60 | Each plaquette (n, μ, ν) has product:
  61 |     U(n,μ) · U(n+e_μ,ν) · U(n+e_μ+e_ν,μ)⁻¹ · U(n+e_ν,ν)⁻¹
  62 | 
  63 | The 3rd and 4th links are **inverted**. By `repCharacter_inv`:
  64 |     χ(g⁻¹) = conj(χ(g)) = χ_{dual}(g)  (via the dual map in the axiom)
  65 | 
  66 | So the character expansion of a plaquette factor with inverted links produces
  67 | **conjugated characters** for the 3rd and 4th links.
  68 | 
  69 | ### 2.4 The reflection symmetry of S_int
  70 | 
  71 | The key symmetry (proved as `interface_action_reflection_symmetric_os_periodic`):
  72 |     S_int(θU) = S_int(U)
  73 | 
  74 | Since θ reflects ALL links (positive ↔ negative, interface → interface with σ), this
  75 | gives:
  76 |     S_int(U⁺, u⁰, U⁻) = S_int(reflect(U⁻), σ(u⁰), reflect(U⁺))
  77 | 
  78 | After change of variables U⁻ = reflect(V⁺):
  79 |     S_int(U⁺, u⁰, reflect(V⁺)) = S_int(V⁺, σ(u⁰), reflect(U⁺))
  80 | 
  81 | This means the interface Boltzmann factor K(U⁺, u⁰, V⁺) = exp(-β·S_int(...)) satisfies:
  82 |     K(U⁺, u⁰, V⁺) = K(V⁺, σ(u⁰), U⁺)
  83 | 
  84 | ### 2.5 The σ reflection on interface links
  85 | 
  86 | For interface sites (signed time = 0), θn = n (since -0 = 0 in ZMod T). So on
  87 | interface links:
  88 | - Time-like (μ=0): (θU)(n, 0) = U(n, 0)⁻¹ — **inverted**
  89 | - Spatial (μ≠0): (θU)(n, μ) = U(n, μ) — **unchanged**
  90 |

 268 | ## 4. Key Insight: The σ Reflection and Interface Time-Like Links
 269 | 
 270 | The fundamental difficulty is the **σ reflection on interface time-like links**.
 271 | When a time-like interface link `g` appears in both the original and reflected
 272 | plaquette factors, the product `χ_s(g) · conj(χ_t(g))` arises. This is NOT
 273 | `|χ(g)|² = χ(g) · conj(χ(g))` (which would be non-negative), but rather a product of
 274 | two different characters, which is complex in general.
 275 | 
 276 | The resolution: `χ_s(g) · conj(χ_t(g))` is a matrix coefficient of `ρ_s ⊗ ρ_t*`,
 277 | which decomposes via CG (with dual representations) into `∑_w N^w_{s,t*} χ_w(g)` with
 278 | `N^w ≥ 0`. After this decomposition, the integral over `g` can be evaluated using
 279 | character orthogonality, giving `∑_w N^w · |∫ f · χ_w|² ≥ 0`.
 280 | 
 281 | This is why the dual map (added to the axiom on 2026-07-30) is essential: it converts
 282 | `conj(χ_t(g))` to `χ_{dual(t)}(g)`, allowing the CG decomposition to combine
 283 | `χ_s(g) · χ_{dual(t)}(g)` into a single character sum.

 335 | To evaluate the u⁰ integral ∫ Ψ_w(u⁰) · A_w(u⁰) · A_w(σ(u⁰)) dμ⁰(u⁰) using character

 337 |

 340 | This is the **L² expansion** (Peter-Weyl theorem: matrix elements of irreducible
 341 | representations form an orthonormal basis of L²(G)). It is NOT provided by the
 342 | current axioms:

 344 | - `peterWeyl_clebschGordan_plaquette` provides the character expansion of the

 348 |   (∫ χ_λ · conj(χ_μ) = δ_{λμ}), which is an **orthogonality** statement, not a
 349 |   **completeness** statement.

 498 | ### 8.1 The key mathematical insight: V⁺ conjugation

 500 | After the change of variables (step b), the transfer matrix kernel is:
 501 | 
 502 |     K(u⁺, u⁰, V⁺) = exp(-β·S⁺(u⁺,u⁰)/2) · exp(-β·S⁺(V⁺,σ(u⁰))/2) · exp(-β·S_int(U⁺,u⁰,reflect(V⁺)))
 503 | 
 504 | The interface plaquettes are of three types (§2.2):
 505 | - **Type A** (base t=0, spatial dirs): involves U⁺ and u⁰ links (NO V⁺ links)
 506 | - **Type B** (base t=T-1, spatial dirs): involves U⁻→V⁺ and u⁰ links
 507 | - **Type C** (base t=0, both spatial): involves u⁰ links only (NO V⁺ links)
 508 | 
 509 | **Key observation**: V⁺ links appear ONLY in type B plaquettes (after the change
 510 | of variables U⁻ = reflect(V⁺)). In type B plaquettes, the V⁺ links appear in:
 511 | - Position 1 (g₁): U⁻_time-like → V⁺_time-like⁻¹ (inverted by reflection).
 512 |   Character: χ_s(V⁺⁻¹) = conj(χ_s(V⁺)). **Conjugated.**
 513 | - Position 4 (g₄⁻¹): U⁻_spatial → V⁺_spatial (not inverted by reflection, but
 514 |   inverted by plaquette). Character: χ_v(V⁺⁻¹) = conj(χ_v(V⁺)). **Conjugated.**
 515 | 
 516 | **ALL V⁺ links have conjugated characters.** This means the character expansion
 517 | of the full kernel K has the form:
 518 | 
 519 |     K(u⁺, u⁰, V⁺) = ∑_w F(w) · Φ_w(U⁺) · Ψ_w(u⁰) · conj(Φ_w(V⁺))
 520 | 
 521 | with F(w) ≥ 0, where Φ_w is a product of characters of U⁺ (resp. V⁺) links,
 522 | and Ψ_w is a product of characters of u⁰ links.
 523 | 
 524 | This is proved by applying `plaquette_product_separable_decomp` (step a) to the
 525 | interface plaquettes, using the fact that the V⁺ links always appear with
 526 | conjugated characters (from the reflection + plaquette inversions).

 528 | ### 8.2 The integral reduction
 529 | 
 530 | With the character expansion K = ∑_w F(w) · Φ_w(U⁺) · Ψ_w(u⁰) · conj(Φ_w(V⁺)),
 531 | the integral ⟨g, Tg⟩ becomes:
 532 | 
 533 |     I = ∑_w F(w) · ∫_{u⁰} Ψ_w(u⁰) · A_w(u⁰) · conj(A_w(σ(u⁰))) dμ⁰(u⁰)
 534 | 
 535 | where A_w(u⁰) = ∫_{u⁺} g(u⁺, u⁰) · Φ_w(U⁺) dμ⁺(u⁺) is the "Fourier coefficient"
 536 | of g with respect to Φ_w (a function of u⁰ alone).
 537 | 
 538 | **Key**: A_w depends on w (through Φ_w). Different w give different A_w.
 539 | 
 540 | ### 8.3 The key challenge: individual terms can be negative
 541 | 
 542 | **Counterexample** (SU(2), single time-like link, σ = inversion):
 543 | - K = χ₀ = 1 (trivial character, PD), A(g) = (ρ_{1/2}(g))₁₂
 544 | - ∫ 1 · (ρ(g))₁₂ · conj((ρ(g⁻¹))₁₂) dμ = ∫ (ρ(g))₁₂ · (ρ(g))₂₁ dμ
 545 | - For SU(2): (ρ(g))₁₂ = b, (ρ(g))₂₁ = -b̄, so the integral = -∫|b|² dμ < 0.
 546 | 
 547 | **Individual terms ∫ Ψ_w · A_w · conj(A_w(σ)) dμ⁰ can be NEGATIVE.**
 548 | The SUM ∑_w F(w) · (individual terms) is ≥ 0, but the proof requires the L²
 549 | expansion and the specific structure of F(w) and A_w.

 551 | ### 8.4 The σ inversion relation for matrix elements
 552 | 
 553 | For unitary representations, ρ(g⁻¹) = ρ(g)ᴴ (conjugate transpose), so:
 554 | 
 555 |     (ρ(σ(g)))_{ij} = (ρ(g⁻¹))_{ij} = conj((ρ(g))_{ji})
 556 | 
 557 | This is the key relation that connects the σ reflection to the matrix-element
 558 | basis. It is derived from `repCharacter_inv` (PositiveDefinite.lean) and the
 559 | unitary property `IsUnitaryRepresentation`.

 561 | ### 8.5 The L² expansion approach
 562 | 
 563 | Expand A_w in the matrix-element basis (using L² completeness from the
 564 | strengthened axiom):
 565 | 
 566 |     A_w(u⁰) = ∑_{λ,i,j} c^w_{λ,i,j} · ∏_l (ρ_{λ_l}(u⁰_l))_{i_l, j_l}
 567 | 
 568 | Then A_w(σ(u⁰)) uses the σ inversion relation:
 569 | 
 570 |     A_w(σ(u⁰)) = ∑_{λ,i,j} c^w_{λ,i,j} ·
 571 |       ∏_{l spatial} (ρ_{λ_l}(u⁰_l))_{i_l, j_l} ·
 572 |       ∏_{l time-like} conj((ρ_{λ_l}(u⁰_l))_{j_l, i_l})

 574 | The integral factorizes (by Fubini, since μ⁰ is a product measure) as a product
 575 | over interface links. For each link l:
 576 | 
 577 | - **Spatial links**: ∫ χ_{w(l)}(g) · (ρ_λ(g))_{ij} · conj((ρ_μ(g))_{kl}) dμ(g)
 578 |   — triple product WITH conjugation. Evaluable by CG + Schur orthogonality.

 581 |   — triple product WITHOUT conjugation. NOT directly evaluable by Schur
 582 |   orthogonality. Requires converting (ρ_μ(g))_{lk} = conj((ρ_μ(g⁻¹))_{kl})
 583 |   and changing variables, giving conj(∫ χ_w · (ρ_λ)_{ji} · (ρ_μ)_{kl} dμ).
 584 |   This is complex in general.

 910 | ### 8.11.4 V⁺ conjugation analysis (2026-08-03 session 4)
 911 | 
 912 | The V⁺ factor `V_w(V⁺)` in the character expansion is the product over
 913 | `interfaceLinkNeg` (negative links) of characters of `reflectPosToNeg(V⁺)`.
 914 | The reflection `reflectPosToNeg` maps negative sites to positive sites via
 915 | `reflectSite`, inverting time-like links (`μ = 0`: `g → g⁻¹`) and keeping
 916 | spatial links (`μ ≠ 0`: `g → g`).

 918 | **Key finding**: the V⁺ factor is NOT simply `conj(Φ_w(V⁺))`. The character
 919 | expansion's `w(l)` assignment (from `plaquette_product_separable_decomp`, step
 920 | (a)) already accounts for the per-plaquette-position inversions (3rd/4th links
 921 | are inverted in the plaquette product, handled by the `dual` map within step
 922 | (a)). The `prod_conj_partition_dual` rewriting in
 923 | `interface_kernel_character_expansion` is a TAUTOLOGY — it rewrites
 924 | `∏_{L_V} χ_{w(l)}(g_l)` as `star(∏_{L_V} χ_{dual(w(l))}(g_l))` = `∏_{L_V}
 925 | χ_{w(l)}(g_l)` (since `star(conj(χ)) = χ` and `χ_{dual(i)} = conj(χ_i)`).
 926 | 
 927 | So the V⁺ factor is `V_w(V⁺) = ∏_{l ∈ interfaceLinkNeg} χ_{w(l)}(g_l)` where
 928 | `g_l = reflectPosToNeg(V⁺) l` and `w(l)` already includes the per-position
 929 | `dual` from step (a). For each negative link `l = (n, μ)`:
 930 | - **Time-like** (`μ = 0`): `g_l = (V⁺ l')⁻¹` (inverted by reflection), so
 931 |   `χ_{w(l)}(g_l) = conj(χ_{w(l)}(V⁺ l'))` — **conjugated** by reflection.
 932 | - **Spatial** (`μ ≠ 0`): `g_l = V⁺ l'` (NOT inverted by reflection), but if `l`
 933 |   appears in an inverted plaquette position (3rd/4th), `w(l)` includes `dual`,

 935 |   **conjugated** by plaquette inversion.

  73 | structure Z4Expectation (N : ℕ) (β : ℝ) (sites : Finset Z4Site) : Type 1 where

  75 |   partitionFunction : ℝ
  76 |   /-- Positivity of the partition function: Z > 0 for β > 0. -/
  77 |   partitionFunctionPos : partitionFunction > 0
  78 |   /--
  79 |   The expectation of an observable F, symbolically:
  80 |       ⟨F⟩ = (1/Z) ∫ F(U) exp(-S_W[U]) dU
  81 |   -/
  82 |   evaluate : (LinkVariable (SU N) Z4Site → ℝ) → ℝ
  83 |   /--

  92 |       Real.exp (-β * wilsonActionFiniteConfigZ4 N β sites cfg)) (productHaarMeasureZ4 N sites)) →
  93 |     evaluate (λ U => a * F U + b * G U) = a * evaluate F + b * evaluate G
  94 |   /--
  95 |   The expectation is normalized: ⟨1⟩ = 1.
  96 |   -/
  97 |   normalization : evaluate (λ _ => 1) = 1
  98 |   /--
  99 |   The expectation is positive: if F ≥ 0 pointwise, then ⟨F⟩ ≥ 0.

 400 | /--
 401 | A function `f : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L) → ℝ` depends only on
 402 | positive-time and interface (time-0) links iff its value is determined by
 403 | the values of the link variable on `positiveSites T L ∪ interfaceSites T L`.
 404 | This is the correct hypothesis for the Osterwalder-Seiler reflection positivity
 405 | theorem: only observables localized in the positive-time region (including the
 406 | interface at time 0) are required to satisfy ⟨θf, f⟩ ≥ 0.
 407 | 
 408 | ⚠️ **Mathematical note**: The lemma `gibbsExpectationPeriodic_reflection_positive`
 409 | as originally stated (without this hypothesis) is **false** in general.  A
 410 | counterexample exists even for β=0 (free theory): take
 411 | `f(U) = a(U(ℓ))·b(U(θℓ)) - a(U(θℓ))·b(U(ℓ))` for a positive-site link ℓ
 412 | and its reflection θℓ.  Then `f·θf = -(f)²` and its integral is strictly negative.
 413 | The hypothesis that `f` depends only on positive+interface links excludes such
 414 | counterexamples.
 415 | -/
 416 | def dependsOnlyOnPosInterface (N T L : ℕ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
 417 |     (f : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L) → ℝ) : Prop :=
 418 |   ∀ (U V : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L)),
 419 |     (∀ (n : PeriodicSite T L) (μ : Fin 4),
 420 |       n ∈ (positiveSites T L ∪ interfaceSites T L) → U.value n μ = V.value n μ) → f U = f V
 421 | 
 422 | /-- Stronger version of `dependsOnlyOnPosInterface` that also excludes temporal
 423 | interface links (direction `μ = 0` at interface sites).
 424 | 
 425 | This is the correct hypothesis for the Osterwalder-Seiler reflection positivity
 426 | theorem.  The weaker `dependsOnlyOnPosInterface` (which allows `f` to depend on
 427 | temporal interface links) is **insufficient**: for `β = 0` (free theory), taking
 428 | `f(g) = Im Tr(g)` for a single temporal interface link `g` gives
 429 | `∫ f(g)·f(g⁻¹) dg = -∫ (Im Tr(g))² dg < 0`, a strictly negative integral.
 430 | The temporal-link inversion `σ` (which inverts `μ = 0` links at the interface)
 431 | is the sole obstacle; restricting `f` to spatial interface links removes it.
 432 | 
 433 | See `docs/transfer_matrix_positivity_design.md` §8.11.36 for the full analysis. -/
 434 | def dependsOnlyOnPosSpatialInterface (N T L : ℕ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
 435 |     (f : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L) → ℝ) : Prop :=
 436 |   ∀ (U V : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L)),
 437 |     (∀ (n : PeriodicSite T L) (μ : Fin 4),
 438 |       n ∈ positiveSites T L ∨ (n ∈ interfaceSites T L ∧ μ ≠ (0 : Fin 4)) →
 439 |       U.value n μ = V.value n μ) → f U = f V
 440 | 
 441 | /-- `dependsOnlyOnPosSpatialInterface` is stronger than `dependsOnlyOnPosInterface`:
 442 | if `f` ignores temporal interface links, it certainly ignores all links outside
 443 | the positive+interface region. -/
 444 | lemma dependsOnlyOnPosSpatialInterface.dependsOnlyOnPosInterface
 445 |     (N T L : ℕ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
 446 |     (f : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L) → ℝ)
 447 |     (hf : dependsOnlyOnPosSpatialInterface N T L f) :
 448 |     dependsOnlyOnPosInterface N T L f := by
 449 |   intro U V hUV
 450 |   apply hf
 451 |   intro n μ hn
 452 |   rcases hn with hpos | ⟨hint, hμ⟩
 453 |   · exact hUV n μ (Finset.mem_union_left _ hpos)
 454 |   · exact hUV n μ (Finset.mem_union_right _ hint)
 455 | 
 456 | /-- **Strongest support condition**: `f` depends only on strictly positive-time links
 457 | (sites with `signedTime > 0`), NOT on any interface links (sites with `signedTime = 0`).
 458 | 
 459 | This is the standard Osterwalder-Schrader OS3 hypothesis: test functions `f` are
 460 | supported in positive time `t > 0`.  It is stronger than `dependsOnlyOnPosSpatialInterface`
 461 | (which allows `f` to depend on spatial interface links at `t = 0`).
 462 | 
 463 | The §8.11.60 analysis showed that the §8.11.58 obstruction (the interface kernel
 464 | `K_{u⁰}` is NOT PD for each `u⁰` because character expansion coefficients `Ψ_w(u⁰)`
 465 | are complex) SURVIVES the change of variables for `dependsOnlyOnPosSpatialInterface`.
 466 | The §8.11.61 analysis identified that the correct proof mechanism requires:
 467 | 
 468 | 1. **`dependsOnlyOnPositive`** (not the weaker `dependsOnlyOnPosSpatialInterface`):
 469 |    so that the interface-link integral gives `δ_{w, trivial}` (unweighted character
 470 |    orthogonality) rather than a weighted integral `∫ f(u⁰_s)²·Ψ_w(u⁰_s) dμ⁰_s` that
 471 |    can be negative.
 472 | 
 473 | 2. **The FULL character expansion** (all plaquettes, not just interface ones):
 474 |    the interface-only expansion gives a "twisted" quadratic form `Σ F(w)·A_w²` that
 475 |    is NOT obviously non-negative (since `A_w` is complex and `Re(A_w²)` can be
 476 |    negative).  The full expansion (bulk + interface) gives `Σ F_full(w)·|Â_w|² ≥ 0`,
 477 |    a standard sum of squared Fourier coefficients with non-negative weights.
 478 | 
 479 | See `docs/transfer_matrix_positivity_design.md` §8.11.61 for the full analysis. -/
 480 | def dependsOnlyOnPositive (N T L : ℕ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
 481 |     (f : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L) → ℝ) : Prop :=
 482 |   ∀ (U V : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L)),
 483 |     (∀ (n : PeriodicSite T L) (μ : Fin 4),
 484 |       n ∈ positiveSites T L → U.value n μ = V.value n μ) → f U = f V
 485 | 
 486 | /-- `dependsOnlyOnPositive` is stronger than `dependsOnlyOnPosSpatialInterface`:
 487 | if `f` depends only on positive-time links (ignoring ALL interface links), then
 488 | in particular it ignores temporal interface links. -/
 489 | lemma dependsOnlyOnPositive.dependsOnlyOnPosSpatialInterface
 490 |     (N T L : ℕ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
 491 |     (f : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L) → ℝ)
 492 |     (hf : dependsOnlyOnPositive N T L f) :
 493 |     dependsOnlyOnPosSpatialInterface N T L f := by
 494 |   intro U V hUV
 495 |   apply hf
 496 |   intro n μ hn
 497 |   exact hUV n μ (Or.inl hn)

 500 | open scoped BigOperators

 502 | /-- Index type for oriented plaquettes on a periodic lattice: (base site, μ, ν). -/
 503 | abbrev PlaquetteIndex (T L : ℕ) : Type := PeriodicSite T L × Fin 4 × Fin 4
 504 | 
 505 | instance (T L : ℕ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L] : Fintype (PlaquetteIndex T L) :=
 506 |   inferInstanceAs (Fintype (PeriodicSite T L × Fin 4 × Fin 4))

 508 | /-- Cyclic permutation of trace for 4 matrices: Tr(ABCD) = Tr(BCDA). -/
 509 | lemma trace_cyclic_four (N : ℕ) (A B C D : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) :
 510 |     Matrix.trace (A * B * C * D) = Matrix.trace (B * C * D * A) := by
 511 |   calc
 512 |     Matrix.trace (A * B * C * D) = Matrix.trace (D * (A * B * C)) := by
 513 |       rw [Matrix.trace_mul_comm (A * B * C) D]
 514 |     _ = Matrix.trace (D * A * B * C) := by noncomm_ring
 515 |     _ = Matrix.trace ((D * A) * (B * C)) := by noncomm_ring
 516 |     _ = Matrix.trace ((B * C) * (D * A)) := Matrix.trace_mul_comm (D * A) (B * C)
 517 |     _ = Matrix.trace (B * C * D * A) := by noncomm_ring
 518 | /-- For A ∈ SU(N), Re Tr(A) = Re Tr(A⁻¹). -/
 519 | lemma trace_re_inv (N : ℕ) (A : SU N) :
 520 |     ((Matrix.trace ((A : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))).re : ℝ) =
 521 |     ((Matrix.trace (((A⁻¹ : SU N) : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))).re : ℝ) := by
 522 |   have hstar : (A⁻¹ : SU N) = (star A : SU N) := by
 523 |     simpa using (Matrix.star_eq_inv (A : SU N)).symm
 524 |   have h_trace_star : Matrix.trace (star ((A : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))) =
 525 |       star (Matrix.trace ((A : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))) := by
 526 |     simp [Matrix.trace, map_sum]
 527 |   calc
 528 |     ((Matrix.trace ((A : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))).re : ℝ) =
 529 |         ((star (Matrix.trace ((A : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)))).re : ℝ) := by simp
 530 |     _ = ((Matrix.trace (star ((A : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)))).re : ℝ) := by
 531 |       simp [h_trace_star]
 532 |     _ = ((Matrix.trace (((A⁻¹ : SU N) : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))).re : ℝ) := by simp [hstar]

 534 | /-- The sum over all oriented plaquettes (n; μ, ν) where all four corners have
 535 | positive signed time. This is the correct positive-time part of the
 536 | Osterwalder-Seiler decomposition. -/
 537 | noncomputable def wilsonActionOSPositive (N T L : ℕ) (β : ℝ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
 538 |     (U : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L)) : ℝ :=
 539 |   ∑ n : PeriodicSite T L, ∑ μ : Fin 4, ∑ ν : Fin 4,
 540 |     if signedTime T n.time > 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time > 0 ∧
 541 |        signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time > 0 ∧
 542 |        signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time > 0 then
 543 |       plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν
 544 |     else 0
 545 | 
 546 | /-- The sum over all oriented plaquettes (n; μ, ν) where all four corners have
 547 | negative signed time. This is the correct negative-time part of the
 548 | Osterwalder-Seiler decomposition. -/
 549 | noncomputable def wilsonActionOSNegative (N T L : ℕ) (β : ℝ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
 550 |     (U : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L)) : ℝ :=
 551 |   ∑ n : PeriodicSite T L, ∑ μ : Fin 4, ∑ ν : Fin 4,
 552 |     if signedTime T n.time < 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time < 0 ∧
 553 |        signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time < 0 ∧
 554 |        signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time < 0 then
 555 |       plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν
 556 |     else 0
 557 | 
 558 | /-- The sum over the remaining oriented plaquettes (those with corners on both sides
 559 | of the time interface). This is the interface part of the
 560 | Osterwalder-Seiler decomposition. -/
 561 | noncomputable def wilsonActionOSInterface (N T L : ℕ) (β : ℝ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
 562 |     (U : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L)) : ℝ :=
 563 |   ∑ n : PeriodicSite T L, ∑ μ : Fin 4, ∑ ν : Fin 4,
 564 |     if ¬ (signedTime T n.time > 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time > 0 ∧
 565 |           signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time > 0 ∧
 566 |           signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time > 0) ∧
 567 |        ¬ (signedTime T n.time < 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time < 0 ∧
 568 |           signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time < 0 ∧
 569 |           signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time < 0) then
 570 |       plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν
 571 |     else 0

 573 | /--
 574 | For each oriented plaquette (n; μ, ν), exactly one of the three conditions holds:
 575 | positive (all corners > 0), negative (all corners < 0), or interface (the rest).
 576 | -/
 577 | lemma plaquette_classification (T L : ℕ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L] (n : PeriodicSite T L) (μ ν : Fin 4) :
 578 |     (signedTime T n.time > 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time > 0 ∧
 579 |      signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time > 0 ∧
 580 |      signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time > 0) ∨
 581 |     (signedTime T n.time < 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time < 0 ∧
 582 |      signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time < 0 ∧
 583 |      signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time < 0) ∨
 584 |     (¬ (signedTime T n.time > 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time > 0 ∧
 585 |         signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time > 0 ∧
 586 |         signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time > 0) ∧
 587 |      ¬ (signedTime T n.time < 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time < 0 ∧
 588 |         signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time < 0 ∧
 589 |         signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time < 0)) := by
 590 |   by_cases hpos : signedTime T n.time > 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time > 0 ∧
 591 |                   signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time > 0 ∧
 592 |                   signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time > 0
 593 |   · exact Or.inl hpos
 594 |   · by_cases hneg : signedTime T n.time < 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time < 0 ∧
 595 |                    signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time < 0 ∧
 596 |                    signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time < 0
 597 |     · exact Or.inr (Or.inl hneg)
 598 |     · exact Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨hpos, hneg⟩)

 606 |     (U : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L)) :
 607 |     wilsonActionFinite N β (Finset.univ : Finset (PeriodicSite T L)) U =
 608 |     wilsonActionOSPositive N T L β U +
 609 |     wilsonActionOSNegative N T L β U +
 610 |     wilsonActionOSInterface N T L β U := by
 611 |   unfold wilsonActionOSPositive wilsonActionOSNegative wilsonActionOSInterface wilsonActionFinite
 612 |   have h_split (n : PeriodicSite T L) (μ ν : Fin 4) : plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν =
 613 |     (if signedTime T n.time > 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time > 0 ∧
 614 |          signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time > 0 ∧
 615 |          signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time > 0 then
 616 |       plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν else 0) +
 617 |     (if signedTime T n.time < 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time < 0 ∧

 619 |          signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time < 0 then

 621 |     (if ¬ (signedTime T n.time > 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time > 0 ∧

 631 |           signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time < 0 ∧

 741 | /-! ### Concrete-to-abstract plaquette-product bridge
 742 | 
 743 | These lemmas connect the *concrete* Wilson action (with its specific sign
 744 | convention `S_p = β(1 - (1/N) Re Tr(U_∂p))`) to the *abstract* plaquette-product
 745 | form `∏_p exp(c · Re Tr(g₁g₂g₃⁻¹g₄⁻¹))` with `c ≥ 0` that the
 746 | `interface_kernel_character_expansion` lemma (in `PeterWeyl.lean`) operates on.
 747 | 
 748 | This is the "exp-of-sum = product-of-exps" step of the KEY GAP identified in
 749 | `docs/transfer_matrix_positivity_design.md` §8.8 (task #46): the concrete
 750 | transfer-matrix kernel `exp(-β·S_OS)` must be rewritten as a product of
 751 | plaquette Boltzmann factors before the abstract character-expansion lemma can
 752 | be applied.  These lemmas are pure algebra (0 axioms, 0 sorries). -/
 753 | 
 754 | /-- The single-plaquette Boltzmann factor `exp(-S_p)` factors as a positive
 755 | constant `exp(-β)` times `exp(c·Re Tr(U_∂p))` with `c = β/N ≥ 0` (for `β ≥ 0`,
 756 | `1 ≤ N`).
 757 | 
 758 | This is the atomic building block of the concrete↔abstract bridge: it shows
 759 | that each plaquette's contribution to the Boltzmann factor matches the abstract
 760 | form `exp(c·Re Tr(g₁g₂g₃⁻¹g₄⁻¹))` (with `c ≥ 0`) up to a positive constant
 761 | that can be absorbed into the overall normalization.  The plaquette product
 762 | `plaquetteProduct = U(n,μ)·U(n+e_μ,ν)·U(n+e_μ+e_ν,μ)⁻¹·U(n+e_ν,ν)⁻¹` already has
 763 | the 3rd/4th links inverted, matching the abstract form.
 764 | 
 765 | This is the same decomposition used internally by `plaquetteContributionPD`
 766 | (in `BoltzmannFactor.lean`); it is extracted here as a standalone equality lemma
 767 | so it can be composed with `exp_neg_wilsonActionFinite_eq_prod` to bridge the
 768 | concrete kernel `exp(-S_W)` to the abstract plaquette-product form. -/
 769 | lemma plaquetteContribution_exp_decomp (N : ℕ) (β : ℝ)
 770 |     {Λ : Type} [AddVector Λ] (U : LinkVariable (SU N) Λ) (n : Λ) (μ ν : Fin 4) :
 771 |     Real.exp (-plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν) =
 772 |     Real.exp (-β) *
 773 |     Real.exp ((β / N) *
 774 |       Complex.re (Matrix.trace ((plaquetteProduct N U n μ ν : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)))) := by
 775 |   unfold plaquetteContribution
 776 |   have h : -(β * (1 - (1 / (N : ℝ)) *
 777 |       Complex.re (Matrix.trace ((plaquetteProduct N U n μ ν : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))))) =
 778 |       (-β) + (β / N) *
 779 |       Complex.re (Matrix.trace ((plaquetteProduct N U n μ ν : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))) := by
 780 |     rw [div_eq_inv_mul]; ring
 781 |   rw [h, Real.exp_add]
 782 | 
 783 | /-- The coupling constant `c = β/N` for the abstract plaquette-product form is
 784 | non-negative when `β ≥ 0` and `1 ≤ N`.  This is the hypothesis `0 ≤ c` required
 785 | by `peterWeyl_clebschGordan_plaquette` and `interface_kernel_character_expansion`. -/
 786 | lemma plaquetteBoltzmann_coupling_nonneg (N : ℕ) (β : ℝ) (hβ : 0 ≤ β) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
 787 |     0 ≤ β / N := by
 788 |   exact div_nonneg hβ (Nat.cast_nonneg N)
 789 | 
 790 | /-- The per-plaquette constant `exp(-β)` is positive. -/
 791 | lemma plaquetteBoltzmann_const_pos (β : ℝ) : 0 < Real.exp (-β) :=
 792 |   Real.exp_pos _
 793 | 
 794 | /-- **Transfer-matrix kernel per-plaquette factorization.** The factor
 795 | `exp(-β·S_p)` (which appears in the transfer-matrix kernel `exp(-β·S_W) =
 796 | ∏ exp(-β·S_p)`, since `osG(U)·osG(θU) = f(U)·f(θU)·exp(-β·S_W)`) decomposes as
 797 | `exp(-β²)·exp((β²/N)·Re Tr(U_∂p))` with coupling `c = β²/N ≥ 0`.
 798 | 
 799 | This is the version needed for the concrete transfer-matrix kernel: the `G`
 800 | function uses `exp(-β·S⁺)` (with the extra β), so the per-plaquette factor is
 801 | `exp(-β·S_p) = exp(-β²)·exp((β²/N)·Re Tr)`, NOT `exp(-S_p)`.  The coupling
 802 | `c = β²/N` is non-negative for all `β` (since `β² ≥ 0`) and `1 ≤ N`. -/
 803 | lemma plaquetteContribution_exp_decomp_tm (N : ℕ) (β : ℝ)
 804 |     {Λ : Type} [AddVector Λ] (U : LinkVariable (SU N) Λ) (n : Λ) (μ ν : Fin 4) :
 805 |     Real.exp (-β * plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν) =
 806 |     Real.exp (-(β * β)) *
 807 |     Real.exp ((β * β / N) *
 808 |       Complex.re (Matrix.trace ((plaquetteProduct N U n μ ν : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)))) := by
 809 |   unfold plaquetteContribution
 810 |   have h : -β * (β * (1 - (1 / (N : ℝ)) *
 811 |       Complex.re (Matrix.trace ((plaquetteProduct N U n μ ν : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))))) =
 812 |       -(β * β) + (β * β / N) *
 813 |       Complex.re (Matrix.trace ((plaquetteProduct N U n μ ν : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))) := by
 814 |     field_simp; ring
 815 |   rw [h, Real.exp_add]
 816 | 
 817 | /-- The transfer-matrix coupling `c = β²/N` is non-negative for all `β` and `1 ≤ N`.
 818 | Unlike `plaquetteBoltzmann_coupling_nonneg`, this does NOT require `β ≥ 0` (since
 819 | `β² ≥ 0` always). -/
 820 | lemma plaquetteBoltzmann_tm_coupling_nonneg (N : ℕ) (β : ℝ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
 821 |     0 ≤ β * β / N := by
 822 |   have hβ : 0 ≤ β * β := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg β, pow_two β]
 823 |   exact div_nonneg hβ (Nat.cast_nonneg N)
 824 | 
 825 | /-- The transfer-matrix per-plaquette constant `exp(-β²)` is positive. -/
 826 | lemma plaquetteBoltzmann_tm_const_pos (β : ℝ) : 0 < Real.exp (-(β * β)) :=
 827 |   Real.exp_pos _

 829 | /-- **exp-of-sum = product-of-exps for the transfer-matrix kernel.** The
 830 | transfer-matrix Boltzmann factor `exp(-β·S_W)` factorises as a product of
 831 | per-plaquette factors `exp(-β·S_p)`:
 832 | 
 833 |     exp(-β·S_W[U]) = ∏_{n ∈ sites} ∏_{μ : Fin 4} ∏_{ν : Fin 4} exp(-β·S_p(n,μ,ν))
 834 | 
 835 | This is the transfer-matrix analogue of `exp_neg_wilsonActionFinite_eq_prod`
 836 | (in `BoltzmannFactor.lean`), with the extra factor of `β` that the `G`/`osG`
 837 | functions introduce.  Pure algebra — no representation theory, no axioms beyond
 838 | the standard three. -/
 839 | lemma exp_neg_beta_wilsonActionFinite_eq_prod (N : ℕ) (β : ℝ)
 840 |     {Λ : Type} [AddVector Λ]
 841 |     (sites : Finset Λ) (U : Lattice.LinkVariable (SU N) Λ) :
 842 |     Real.exp (-β * Lattice.wilsonActionFinite N β sites U) =
 843 |     ∏ n ∈ sites, ∏ μ : Fin 4, ∏ ν : Fin 4,
 844 |       Real.exp (-β * Lattice.plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν) := by
 845 |   simp only [Lattice.wilsonActionFinite, ← Finset.sum_neg_distrib, Real.exp_sum,
 846 |     Finset.mul_sum]

 856 | /-! ### G3: Interface plaquette enumeration
 857 | 
 858 | The third piece of the concrete↔abstract bridge (§8.11 of
 859 | `docs/transfer_matrix_positivity_design.md`): restrict the product to
 860 | *interface* plaquettes only.  The interface action `S_OS_int` is defined as
 861 | `∑ (if isInterface then S_p else 0)`, so `exp(-β·S_int) = ∏ (if isInterface
 862 | then exp(-β·S_p) else 1)` by exp-of-sum + if-splitting.  Non-interface
 863 | plaquettes contribute a factor of 1, so the product is effectively over
 864 | interface plaquettes only.  Pure algebra — 0 sorries, 0 custom axioms. -/
 865 | 
 866 | /-- The interface plaquette predicate: a plaquette `(n, μ, ν)` is an "interface
 867 | plaquette" iff its four corners do NOT all have positive signed time AND do NOT
 868 | all have negative signed time (i.e., the corners straddle the time interface).
 869 | This matches the condition in `wilsonActionOSInterface`.  Defined as an
 870 | abbreviation so it unfolds to the inline condition (matching the `Decidable`
 871 | instance used by `wilsonActionOSInterface`). -/
 872 | abbrev isInterfacePlaquette (T L : ℕ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
 873 |     (n : PeriodicSite T L) (μ ν : Fin 4) : Prop :=
 874 |   ¬ (signedTime T n.time > 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time > 0 ∧
 875 |      signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time > 0 ∧
 876 |      signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time > 0) ∧
 877 |   ¬ (signedTime T n.time < 0 ∧ signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ).time < 0 ∧
 878 |      signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L n μ) ν).time < 0 ∧
 879 |      signedTime T (addVectorPeriodic T L n ν).time < 0)
 880 | 
 881 | /-- `wilsonActionOSInterface` equals the sum over all plaquettes with the
 882 | interface predicate as the if-condition.  This is by definition (the condition
 883 | in `wilsonActionOSInterface` is exactly `isInterfacePlaquette`). -/
 884 | lemma wilsonActionOSInterface_eq (N T L : ℕ) (β : ℝ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
 885 |     (U : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L)) :
 886 |     wilsonActionOSInterface N T L β U =
 887 |     ∑ n : PeriodicSite T L, ∑ μ : Fin 4, ∑ ν : Fin 4,
 888 |       (if isInterfacePlaquette T L n μ ν then plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν else 0) := by
 889 |   unfold wilsonActionOSInterface isInterfacePlaquette
 890 |   rfl
 891 | 
 892 | /-- The interface action is uniformly bounded: `|S_int| ≤ #(PeriodicSite T L)·32·|β|`.
 893 | 
 894 | Each plaquette contribution satisfies `|plaquetteContribution| ≤ 2|β|`
 895 | (`plaquetteContribution_bounded`), and the interface action is a sum of at most
 896 | `#(PeriodicSite T L)·16` such terms (the `if isInterfacePlaquette` selects a subset).
 897 | This gives `|S_int| ≤ #(PeriodicSite T L)·16·2|β| = #(PeriodicSite T L)·32·|β|`.
 898 | 
 899 | This is ingredient 2 of the integrability discharge (design doc §8.11.10): it
 900 | provides a uniform upper bound on `|S_int|`, hence a positive lower bound
 901 | `exp(-β·S_int) ≥ exp(-|β|·#(PeriodicSite T L)·32·|β|) > 0`. 0 sorries, 0 custom axioms. -/
 902 | lemma wilsonActionOSInterface_bounded (N T L : ℕ) (β : ℝ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
 903 |     (U : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L)) :
 904 |     |wilsonActionOSInterface N T L β U| ≤ (Fintype.card (PeriodicSite T L) * 32) * |β| := by
 905 |   rw [wilsonActionOSInterface_eq]
 906 |   -- Each term is bounded: |if c then pc else 0| ≤ 2|β|
 907 |   have h_bound : ∀ n μ ν,
 908 |       |(if isInterfacePlaquette T L n μ ν then plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν else 0)| ≤
 909 |         2 * |β| := by
 910 |     intro n μ ν
 911 |     by_cases h : isInterfacePlaquette T L n μ ν
 912 |     · rw [if_pos h]; exact plaquetteContribution_bounded N β U n μ ν
 913 |     · rw [if_neg h]; simp
 914 |   -- Upper bound: each term ≤ 2|β|
 915 |   have h_upper : ∀ n μ ν,
 916 |       (if isInterfacePlaquette T L n μ ν then plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν else 0) ≤
 917 |         2 * |β| := fun n μ ν => (abs_le.mp (h_bound n μ ν)).2
 918 |   -- Lower bound: each term ≥ -(2|β|)
 919 |   have h_lower : ∀ n μ ν,
 920 |       -(2 * |β|) ≤
 921 |         (if isInterfacePlaquette T L n μ ν then plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν else 0) :=
 922 |     fun n μ ν => (abs_le.mp (h_bound n μ ν)).1
 923 |   -- S ≤ ∑ n μ ν 2|β|
 924 |   have h_S_upper : (∑ n : PeriodicSite T L, ∑ μ : Fin 4, ∑ ν : Fin 4,
 925 |       (if isInterfacePlaquette T L n μ ν then plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν else 0)) ≤
 926 |     ∑ n : PeriodicSite T L, ∑ μ : Fin 4, ∑ ν : Fin 4, 2 * |β| := by
 927 |     apply Finset.sum_le_sum; intro n _
 928 |     apply Finset.sum_le_sum; intro μ _
 929 |     apply Finset.sum_le_sum; intro ν _
 930 |     exact h_upper n μ ν
 931 |   -- -(∑ n μ ν 2|β|) ≤ S
 932 |   have h_S_lower : (∑ n : PeriodicSite T L, ∑ μ : Fin 4, ∑ ν : Fin 4, -(2 * |β|)) ≤
 933 |     (∑ n : PeriodicSite T L, ∑ μ : Fin 4, ∑ ν : Fin 4,
 934 |       (if isInterfacePlaquette T L n μ ν then plaquetteContribution N β U n μ ν else 0)) := by
 935 |     apply Finset.sum_le_sum; intro n _
 936 |     apply Finset.sum_le_sum; intro μ _
 937 |     apply Finset.sum_le_sum; intro ν _
 938 |     exact h_lower n μ ν
 939 |   -- Constant sums
 940 |   have h_const : (∑ n : PeriodicSite T L, ∑ μ : Fin 4, ∑ ν : Fin 4, 2 * |β|) =
 941 |       (Fintype.card (PeriodicSite T L) * 32) * |β| := by
 942 |     have h_ν : ∑ ν : Fin 4, (2 * |β| : ℝ) = 8 * |β| := by
 943 |       rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]; ring
 944 |     have h_μ : ∑ μ : Fin 4, (8 * |β| : ℝ) = 32 * |β| := by
 945 |       rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]; ring
 946 |     have h_n : ∑ n : PeriodicSite T L, (32 * |β| : ℝ) =
 947 |         Fintype.card (PeriodicSite T L) * (32 * |β|) := by
 948 |       rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]
 949 |     rw [h_ν, h_μ, h_n]; ring
 950 |   have h_const_neg : (∑ n : PeriodicSite T L, ∑ μ : Fin 4, ∑ ν : Fin 4, -(2 * |β|)) =
 951 |       -((Fintype.card (PeriodicSite T L) * 32) * |β|) := by
 952 |     have h_ν : ∑ ν : Fin 4, (-(2 * |β|) : ℝ) = -(8 * |β|) := by
 953 |       rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]; ring
 954 |     have h_μ : ∑ μ : Fin 4, (-(8 * |β|) : ℝ) = -(32 * |β|) := by
 955 |       rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]; ring
 956 |     have h_n : ∑ n : PeriodicSite T L, (-(32 * |β|) : ℝ) =
 957 |         -(Fintype.card (PeriodicSite T L) * (32 * |β|)) := by
 958 |       rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]; ring
 959 |     rw [h_ν, h_μ, h_n]; ring
 960 |   -- |S| ≤ C
 961 |   rw [h_const] at h_S_upper
 962 |   rw [h_const_neg] at h_S_lower
 963 |   exact abs_le.mpr ⟨h_S_lower, h_S_upper⟩

1066 | /-! ### Concrete link/plaquette structures for the character expansion
1067 | 
1068 | These definitions set up the concrete combinatorial data needed to apply the
1069 | abstract `interface_kernel_character_expansion` (in `PeterWeyl.lean`) to the
1070 | concrete periodic lattice.  This is sub-step (i) of Lemma 2
1071 | (`transfer_matrix_integral_reduction`) in
1072 | `docs/transfer_matrix_positivity_design.md` §8.8: identifying the link
1073 | partition `L = L_U ⊔ L_0 ⊔ L_V` (U⁺/u⁰/V⁺ links) for the concrete lattice.
1074 | 
1075 | All definitions and lemmas here are pure combinatorics — 0 sorries, 0 custom
1076 | axioms. -/

1078 | /-- The j-th link of a plaquette `(n, μ, ν)`.  The four links of the plaquette
1079 | product `U(n,μ) · U(n+e_μ,ν) · U(n+e_μ+e_ν,μ)⁻¹ · U(n+e_ν,ν)⁻¹` are:
1080 |   - j=0: `(n, μ)`           — the link `U(n, μ)`
1081 |   - j=1: `(n+e_μ, ν)`       — the link `U(n+e_μ, ν)`
1082 |   - j=2: `(n+e_μ+e_ν, μ)`   — the link `U(n+e_μ+e_ν, μ)`, **inverted** in the product
1083 |   - j=3: `(n+e_ν, ν)`       — the link `U(n+e_ν, ν)`, **inverted** in the product
1084 | This matches the definition of `plaquetteProduct` in `Lattice.lean`. -/
1085 | def plaquetteLinkIdx (T L : ℕ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
1086 |     (p : PlaquetteIndex T L) (j : Fin 4) : PeriodicSite T L × Fin 4 :=
1087 |   match j with
1088 |   | 0 => (p.1, p.2.1)
1089 |   | 1 => (addVectorPeriodic T L p.1 p.2.1, p.2.2)
1090 |   | 2 => (addVectorPeriodic T L (addVectorPeriodic T L p.1 p.2.1) p.2.2, p.2.1)
1091 |   | 3 => (addVectorPeriodic T L p.1 p.2.2, p.2.2)
1092 | 
1093 | /-- The plaquette product equals the product of link variables at the four
1094 | plaquette links (with the 3rd and 4th inverted).  This connects the concrete
1095 | `plaquetteProduct` to the abstract form
1096 | `g(links p 0)·g(links p 1)·g(links p 2)⁻¹·g(links p 3)⁻¹` that
1097 | `interface_kernel_character_expansion` operates on. -/
1098 | lemma plaquetteProduct_eq_linkIdx (N T L : ℕ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
1099 |     (U : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L)) (p : PlaquetteIndex T L) :
1100 |     plaquetteProduct N U p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2 =
1101 |     U.value (plaquetteLinkIdx T L p 0).1 (plaquetteLinkIdx T L p 0).2 *
1102 |     U.value (plaquetteLinkIdx T L p 1).1 (plaquetteLinkIdx T L p 1).2 *
1103 |     (U.value (plaquetteLinkIdx T L p 2).1 (plaquetteLinkIdx T L p 2).2)⁻¹ *
1104 |     (U.value (plaquetteLinkIdx T L p 3).1 (plaquetteLinkIdx T L p 3).2)⁻¹ := by
1105 |   unfold plaquetteLinkIdx plaquetteProduct
1106 |   rfl

1147 |     (p : InterfacePlaquette T L) (j : Fin 4) : InterfaceLink T L :=
1148 |   ⟨plaquetteLinkIdx T L p.val j, by
1149 |     simp only [interfacePlaqLinkFinset, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,

1151 |     exact ⟨p, j, rfl⟩⟩

1155 | `interface_kernel_character_expansion`. -/
1156 | lemma interfaceLinkAssign_surj (T L : ℕ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L] :
1157 |     ∀ l : InterfaceLink T L, ∃ p j, interfaceLinkAssign T L p j = l := by
1158 |   intro l
1159 |   have hl : l.val ∈ interfacePlaqLinkFinset T L := l.prop
1160 |   simp only [interfacePlaqLinkFinset, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
1161 |     Prod.exists, exists_prop] at hl
1162 |   obtain ⟨p, j, hj⟩ := hl
1163 |   refine ⟨p, j, ?_⟩
1164 |   simp only [interfaceLinkAssign, Subtype.mk_eq_mk, hj]

1175 |     Measurable (fun (U : LinkVariable (SU N) (PeriodicSite T L)) => interfaceLinkVar N T L U l) := by
1176 |   dsimp [interfaceLinkVar]

1216 | /-- Trichotomy of `signedTime`: exactly one of `> 0`, `= 0`, `< 0` holds. -/

1218 |     signedTime T t > 0 ∨ signedTime T t = 0 ∨ signedTime T t < 0 := by
1219 |   omega

1221 | /-- The three link sets are pairwise disjoint and cover all interface links. -/
1222 | lemma interfaceLinkPartition_disjoint_cover (T L : ℕ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L] :
1223 |     Disjoint (interfaceLinkPos T L) (interfaceLinkInt T L) ∧
1224 |     Disjoint (interfaceLinkPos T L ∪ interfaceLinkInt T L) (interfaceLinkNeg T L) ∧
1225 |     interfaceLinkPos T L ∪ interfaceLinkInt T L ∪ interfaceLinkNeg T L = Finset.univ := by
1226 |   refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
1227 |   · -- Disjoint pos int
1228 |     refine Finset.disjoint_left.mpr (fun l hl hl' => ?_)
1229 |     rw [interfaceLinkPos, Finset.mem_filter] at hl
1230 |     rw [interfaceLinkInt, Finset.mem_filter] at hl'
1231 |     obtain ⟨_, hpos⟩ := hl
1232 |     obtain ⟨_, hint⟩ := hl'
1233 |     rw [hint] at hpos
1234 |     exact lt_irrefl _ hpos
1235 |   · -- Disjoint (pos ∪ int) neg
1236 |     refine Finset.disjoint_left.mpr (fun l hl hl' => ?_)
1237 |     rw [interfaceLinkNeg, Finset.mem_filter] at hl'
1238 |     obtain ⟨_, hneg⟩ := hl'
1239 |     rcases Finset.mem_union.mp hl with h | h
1240 |     · rw [interfaceLinkPos, Finset.mem_filter] at h
1241 |       obtain ⟨_, hpos⟩ := h
1242 |       exact lt_irrefl _ (lt_of_lt_of_le hpos (le_of_lt hneg))
1243 |     · rw [interfaceLinkInt, Finset.mem_filter] at h
1244 |       obtain ⟨_, hint⟩ := h
1245 |       rw [hint] at hneg
1246 |       exact lt_irrefl _ hneg
1247 |   · -- Cover
1248 |     ext l
1249 |     simp only [interfaceLinkPos, interfaceLinkInt, interfaceLinkNeg, Finset.mem_union,
1250 |       Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
1251 |     refine ⟨fun _ => trivial, fun _ => ?_⟩
1252 |     rcases signedTime_trichotomy T l.val.1.time with h | h | h
1253 |     · exact Or.inl (Or.inl h)
1254 |     · exact Or.inl (Or.inr h)
1255 |     · exact Or.inr h

1385 | lemma prod_allLinkPos_eq_prod_finiteLinkIndex (T L : ℕ) [NeZero T] [NeZero L]
1386 |     {α : Type*} [CommMonoid α] (f : (PeriodicSite T L × Fin 4) → α) :

1388 |     ∏ (l : FiniteLinkIndex (PeriodicSite T L) (positiveSites T L)), f l.val :=

1428 |     (hU : ∀ i, IsUnitaryRepresentation (ρ i))
1429 |     (hIrr : ∀ i, IsIrreducible (ρ i))
1430 |     (σ_0 : ι) (hσ_0_dims : dims σ_0 = 1) (hσ_0_trivial : ∀ g, (ρ σ_0 g) = 1)
1431 |     (w : (PeriodicSite T L × Fin 4) → ι) :
1432 |     ∫ (cfg : FiniteLinkConfig N (PeriodicSite T L) (interfaceSites T L)),
1433 |       ∏ (l : FiniteLinkIndex (PeriodicSite T L) (interfaceSites T L)),
1434 |         repCharacter (ρ (w l.val)) (cfg l)
1435 |       ∂ (productHaarMeasure N (PeriodicSite T L) (interfaceSites T L)) =
1436 |       ∏ (l : FiniteLinkIndex (PeriodicSite T L) (interfaceSites T L)),

1448 |   -- productHaarMeasure = Measure.pi (fun _ => μ) by definition.

1450 |       MeasureTheory.Measure.pi (fun _ : FiniteLinkIndex (PeriodicSite T L) (interfaceSites T L) => μ) from by
1451 |     dsimp [productHaarMeasure, μ]]

1454 |     (FiniteLinkIndex (PeriodicSite T L) (interfaceSites T L))

3314 | /-- **Axiom (Transfer-matrix positivity).**
3315 | 
3316 | For `f` depending only on positive-time and **spatial** interface links (i.e.
3317 | `dependsOnlyOnPosSpatialInterface`), the integral `∫ G(U)·G(θU) dμ₀ ≥ 0`,
3318 | where `G = osG` is the Osterwalder-Seiler Boltzmann factor and `θ` is the
3319 | time-reflection.
3320 | 
3321 | ⚠️ **The hypothesis `dependsOnlyOnPosSpatialInterface` (not the weaker
3322 | `dependsOnlyOnPosInterface`) is essential.**  The weaker condition allows `f`
3323 | to depend on temporal interface links (`μ = 0` at `t = 0`), for which the
3324 | axiom is **false**: for `β = 0`, `f(g) = Im Tr(g)` on a single temporal
3325 | interface link gives `∫ f(g)·f(g⁻¹) dg = -∫ (Im Tr(g))² dg < 0`.  The
3326 | temporal-link inversion `σ` (which inverts `μ = 0` links at the interface)
3327 | is the sole obstacle.  See `docs/transfer_matrix_positivity_design.md`
3328 | §8.11.36.
3329 | 
3330 | This is the positivity of the transfer matrix `T` constructed from the
3331 | plaquette Boltzmann factor.  The mathematical justification is:
3332 | 
3333 | 1. The plaquette Boltzmann factor `exp(c·Re Tr(g₁g₂g₃g₄))` is a
3334 |    positive-definite function on `SU(N)⁴` — this is proved (from the
3335 |    Peter-Weyl / Clebsch-Gordan axiom) in `PeterWeyl.lean` as
3336 |    `plaquetteBoltzmannPD`.
3337 | 2. Positive-definiteness of the plaquette factor implies that the transfer
3338 |    matrix `T` (which integrates out the negative-time links with the
3339 |    reflection kernel) is a positive operator on `L²(SU(N)^{spatial})`.
3340 |    The temporal interface links are integrated out as part of the transfer
3341 |    matrix kernel (Lüscher decomposition `T = V^{1/2}·U·V^{1/2}`), avoiding
3342 |    the `σ` twist.
3343 | 3. The identity `∫ G(U)·G(θU) dμ₀ = ∫ g(u)·(Tg)(u) dμ⁺⁰` (proved in
3344 |    `TransferMatrix.lean` as `integral_G_thetaG_eq_inner_g_Tg`) then gives
3345 |    `∫ G·G(θU) ≥ 0` from the positivity of `T`.
3346 | 
3347 | Steps 2–3 require the full transfer-matrix construction (measure-theoretic
3348 | factorization of the product Haar measure, Fubini, and the character-expansion
3349 | argument).  The positive-definiteness of the plaquette factor (step 1) is the
3350 | key input and is proved in `PeterWeyl.lean`; the remaining measure theory is
3351 | axiomatized here.  See `docs/found_issues.md` §3 and `docs/gap_analysis.md`.
3352 | 
3353 | Note: a gauge-invariance hypothesis (`IsGaugeInvariant N f`) was previously
3354 | included (session 62) based on the §8.11.51 analysis, but has been REMOVED
3355 | (session 65) after §8.11.53 showed that analysis was flawed — the positivity
3356 | holds for ALL `f` with `dependsOnlyOnPosSpatialInterface`, not just
3357 | gauge-invariant `f`.  See `docs/transfer_matrix_positivity_design.md` §8.11.53. -/

314 | lemma PositiveDefiniteKernel.one (X : Type*) :
315 |     PositiveDefiniteKernel (fun (_ _ : X) => (1 : ℂ)) := by
316 |   apply PositiveDefiniteKernel.of_quadratic_form
317 |   intro s c
318 |   have hsum : (∑ i ∈ s, ∑ j ∈ s, c i * conj (c j) * 1) =
319 |       conj (∑ i ∈ s, c i) * (∑ i ∈ s, c i) := by
320 |     simp only [mul_one]
321 |     rw [← Finset.sum_mul_sum, ← map_sum (starRingEnd ℂ) c s, mul_comm]
322 |   rw [hsum, ← Complex.normSq_eq_conj_mul_self]
323 |   exact Complex.zero_le_real.mpr (Complex.normSq_nonneg _)

325 | /-- **Schur product theorem for Mercer-PD kernels.**  The pointwise product of
326 | two Mercer-PD kernels is again Mercer-PD.  With the `Matrix.PosSemidef`-based
327 | definition, this is a direct application of `Matrix.PosSemidef.hadamard` (the
328 | Schur product theorem for positive-semidefinite matrices): the Hadamard product
329 | of the two finite submatrices is positive-semidefinite, and `Matrix.hadamard`
330 | is pointwise multiplication by definition. -/
331 | lemma PositiveDefiniteKernel.mul {X : Type*} {K1 K2 : X → X → ℂ}
332 |     (hK1 : PositiveDefiniteKernel K1) (hK2 : PositiveDefiniteKernel K2) :
333 |     PositiveDefiniteKernel (fun x y => K1 x y * K2 x y) := by
334 |   intro s
335 |   exact Matrix.PosSemidef.hadamard (hK1 s) (hK2 s)

337 | /-- Non-negative scaling preserves Mercer-PD (via `of_quadratic_form`). -/
338 | lemma PositiveDefiniteKernel.smul_nonneg {X : Type*} {K : X → X → ℂ} {r : ℝ}
339 |     (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hK : PositiveDefiniteKernel K) :
340 |     PositiveDefiniteKernel (fun x y => (r : ℂ) * K x y) := by
341 |   apply PositiveDefiniteKernel.of_quadratic_form
342 |   intro s c
343 |   have h := hK.quadratic_form_nonneg s c
344 |   have hsum : (∑ i ∈ s, ∑ j ∈ s, c i * conj (c j) * ((r : ℂ) * K i j)) =
345 |       (r : ℂ) * (∑ i ∈ s, ∑ j ∈ s, c i * conj (c j) * K i j) := by
346 |     simp [Finset.mul_sum, mul_assoc, mul_comm, mul_left_comm]
347 |   rw [hsum]
348 |   have h_nonneg_complex : (0 : ℂ) ≤ (r : ℂ) := by
349 |     rw [Complex.nonneg_iff]; constructor
350 |     · simpa using hr
351 |     · simp
352 |   exact mul_nonneg h_nonneg_complex h

354 | /-- **Finite product of Mercer-PD kernels is Mercer-PD** (n-ary Schur product). -/
355 | lemma PositiveDefiniteKernel.finprod {ι X : Type*} (s : Finset ι)
356 |     (f : ι → X → X → ℂ) (hf : ∀ i ∈ s, PositiveDefiniteKernel (f i)) :
357 |     PositiveDefiniteKernel (fun x y => ∏ i ∈ s, f i x y) := by
358 |   classical
359 |   induction s using Finset.induction_on with
360 |   | empty =>
361 |     simp only [Finset.prod_empty]
362 |     exact PositiveDefiniteKernel.one X
363 |   | insert a s ha ih =>
364 |     have hPDa : PositiveDefiniteKernel (f a) := hf a (Finset.mem_insert_self a s)
365 |     have hPDs : PositiveDefiniteKernel (fun x y => ∏ i ∈ s, f i x y) :=
366 |       ih (fun i hi => hf i (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hi))
367 |     have heq : (fun x y => ∏ i ∈ insert a s, f i x y) =
368 |         fun x y => f a x y * ∏ i ∈ s, f i x y := by
369 |       funext x y; rw [Finset.prod_insert ha]
370 |     rw [heq]
371 |     exact PositiveDefiniteKernel.mul hPDa hPDs

373 | /-- **Mercer-PD is preserved by composition with a function on both arguments.**
374 | If `K` is a Mercer-PD kernel on `Y` and `f : X → Y`, then
375 | `fun x y => K (f x) (f y)` is a Mercer-PD kernel on `X`. -/
376 | lemma PositiveDefiniteKernel.comp {X Y : Type*} {K : Y → Y → ℂ}
377 |     (hK : PositiveDefiniteKernel K) (f : X → Y) :
378 |     PositiveDefiniteKernel (fun x y => K (f x) (f y)) := by
379 |   apply PositiveDefiniteKernel.of_quadratic_form
380 |   intro s c
381 |   exact hK.sum_nonneg_of_map s f c

383 | /-- **Continuity of a Mercer-PD kernel is preserved by composition with a
384 | continuous function on both arguments.** -/
385 | lemma PositiveDefiniteKernel.continuous_comp {X Y : Type*}
386 |     [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
387 |     {K : Y → Y → ℂ} (hK_cont : Continuous (Function.uncurry K))
388 |     (f : X → Y) (hf_cont : Continuous f) :
389 |     Continuous (Function.uncurry (fun x y => K (f x) (f y))) := by
390 |   have hf_fst : Continuous (fun p : X × X => f p.1) := hf_cont.comp continuous_fst
391 |   have hf_snd : Continuous (fun p : X × X => f p.2) := hf_cont.comp continuous_snd
392 |   have hf_prod : Continuous (fun p : X × X => (f p.1, f p.2)) :=
393 |     Continuous.prodMk hf_fst hf_snd
394 |   exact hK_cont.comp hf_prod

396 | /-- **A continuous Mercer-PD kernel on a compact space defines a positive
397 | integral operator.**
398 | 
399 | For a compact (pseudo)metric space `X` with probability measure `μ`, a
400 | continuous kernel `K` that is positive-definite in the Mercer sense, and a
401 | continuous function `f`, the integral
402 | `∫∫ f(x) * conj(f(y)) * K(x, y) dμ dμ ≥ 0`.
403 | 
404 | The proof approximates the integral by Riemann sums (each non-negative by
405 | `PositiveDefiniteKernel.sum_nonneg_of_map`) and controls the error via
406 | uniform continuity on the compact space `X × X`.  No group structure is
407 | needed. -/
408 | lemma PositiveDefiniteKernel.integralOperator_nonneg
409 |     {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X]
410 |     [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [SecondCountableTopology X]
411 |     (μ : Measure X) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
412 |     {K : X → X → ℂ} (hK : PositiveDefiniteKernel K)
413 |     (hK_cont : Continuous (Function.uncurry K))
414 |     {f : X → ℂ} (hf_cont : Continuous f) :
415 |     0 ≤ ∫ x, ∫ y, f x * conj (f y) * K x y ∂μ ∂μ := by
416 |   let F : X × X → ℂ := fun p => f p.1 * conj (f p.2) * K p.1 p.2
417 |   have hF_cont : Continuous F := by
418 |     have h_fst : Continuous (fun p : X × X => f p.1) := hf_cont.comp continuous_fst
419 |     have h_snd : Continuous (fun p : X × X => f p.2) := hf_cont.comp continuous_snd
420 |     have h_conj_snd : Continuous (fun p : X × X => conj (f p.2)) :=
421 |       Complex.continuous_conj.comp h_snd
422 |     have h_K : Continuous (fun p : X × X => K p.1 p.2) := hK_cont
423 |     convert Continuous.mul (Continuous.mul h_fst h_conj_snd) h_K using 1
424 |     ext p; rfl
425 |   haveI : CompactSpace (X × X) := inferInstance
426 |   have hF_unif : UniformContinuous F :=
427 |     CompactSpace.uniformContinuous_of_continuous hF_cont
428 |   have hF_aes : AEStronglyMeasurable F (μ.prod μ) :=
429 |     Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable_of_compactSpace hF_cont
430 |   have hF_bdd : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ z : X × X, ‖F z‖ ≤ C := by
431 |     have h_range_compact : IsCompact (Set.range F) := by
432 |       rw [← Set.image_univ]
433 |       exact isCompact_univ.image hF_cont
434 |     obtain ⟨C, hCpos, hC⟩ := h_range_compact.isBounded.exists_pos_norm_le
435 |     exact ⟨C, hCpos.le, fun z => hC (F z) (Set.mem_range_self _)⟩
436 |   obtain ⟨C, hCnn, hC⟩ := hF_bdd
437 |   have hF_int : Integrable F (μ.prod μ) := by
438 |     apply Integrable.of_bound hF_aes C
439 |     filter_upwards with z using hC z
440 |   have hFub : ∫ z, F z ∂(μ.prod μ) = ∫ x, ∫ y, f x * conj (f y) * K x y ∂μ ∂μ := by
441 |     rw [integral_prod F hF_int]
442 |   rw [← hFub]
443 |   set I : ℂ := ∫ z, F z ∂(μ.prod μ)
444 |   have hkey : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ S : ℂ, 0 ≤ S ∧ ‖I - S‖ ≤ ε := by
445 |     intro ε εpos
446 |     obtain ⟨δ, δpos, hδ⟩ := Metric.uniformContinuous_iff.mp hF_unif ε εpos
447 |     obtain ⟨t, _, ht_fin, ht_cover⟩ :=
448 |       finite_cover_balls_of_compact (isCompact_univ : IsCompact (Set.univ : Set X)) (half_pos δpos)
449 |     let ts : Finset X := ht_fin.toFinset
450 |     have hts_eq : ↑ts = t := ht_fin.coe_toFinset
451 |     let n := ts.card
452 |     let e : Fin n ≃ ↥ts := ts.equivFin.symm
453 |     let x : Fin n → X := fun i => (e i : X)
454 |     let B : Fin n → Set X := fun i => ball (x i) (δ / 2)
455 |     have hA_disjoint : Pairwise (Disjoint on disjointed B) := disjoint_disjointed B
456 |     have hA_cover : (Set.univ : Set X) ⊆ ⋃ (i : Fin n), disjointed B i := by
457 |       rw [iUnion_disjointed]
458 |       intro g hg
459 |       simp only [Set.mem_iUnion]
460 |       have hg' := ht_cover hg
461 |       simp only [Set.mem_iUnion₂] at hg'
462 |       obtain ⟨xg, hxg, hg_ball⟩ := hg'
463 |       have hxg_ts : xg ∈ ts := by
464 |         have : xg ∈ (↑ts : Set X) := hts_eq.symm ▸ hxg
465 |         exact Finset.mem_coe.mp this
466 |       obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := (Equiv.surjective e) ⟨xg, hxg_ts⟩
467 |       refine ⟨i, ?_⟩
468 |       have hxi : x i = xg := by simp only [x, hi]
469 |       simp only [B, hxi]
470 |       exact hg_ball
471 |     have hA_meas : ∀ (i : Fin n), MeasurableSet (disjointed B i) := by
472 |       intro i
473 |       rw [disjointed_apply, Finset.sup_set_eq_biUnion]
474 |       exact MeasurableSet.diff isOpen_ball.measurableSet
475 |         (Finset.measurableSet_biUnion _ (fun j _ => isOpen_ball.measurableSet))
476 |     let c : Fin n → ℂ := fun i => f (x i) * ((μ.real (disjointed B i)) : ℂ)
477 |     refine ⟨∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) * K (x i) (x j), ?_, ?_⟩
478 |     · exact hK.sum_nonneg_of_map Finset.univ x c
479 |     · have hCover : (Set.univ : Set (X × X)) =
480 |         ⋃ (ij : Fin n × Fin n), disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2 := by
481 |         rw [Set.iUnion_prod]
482 |         have hU : (⋃ i, disjointed B i) = (Set.univ : Set X) :=
483 |           (Set.subset_univ _).antisymm hA_cover
484 |         simp only [hU, Set.univ_prod_univ]
485 |       have hDisj : Pairwise (Disjoint on
486 |           fun ij : Fin n × Fin n => disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2) := by
487 |         intro ij ij' hij
488 |         simp only [Function.onFun]
489 |         rw [Set.disjoint_prod]
490 |         by_cases h1 : ij.1 = ij'.1
491 |         · right; exact hA_disjoint (fun heq => hij (Prod.ext h1 heq))
492 |         · left; exact hA_disjoint h1
493 |       have hMeas' : ∀ (ij : Fin n × Fin n),
494 |           MeasurableSet (disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2) :=
495 |         fun ij => MeasurableSet.prod (hA_meas ij.1) (hA_meas ij.2)
496 |       have hInt' : ∀ (ij : Fin n × Fin n),
497 |           IntegrableOn F (disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2) (μ.prod μ) :=
498 |         fun ij => hF_int.integrableOn
499 |       have hI_part : I = ∑ (ij : Fin n × Fin n),
500 |           ∫ z in disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2, F z ∂(μ.prod μ) := by
501 |         rw [show I = ∫ z in Set.univ, F z ∂(μ.prod μ) from setIntegral_univ.symm, hCover]
502 |         exact integral_iUnion_fintype hMeas' hDisj hInt'
503 |       have h_term : ∀ (ij : Fin n × Fin n),
504 |           c ij.1 * conj (c ij.2) * K (x ij.1) (x ij.2) =
505 |           ∫ z in disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2, F (x ij.1, x ij.2) ∂(μ.prod μ) := by
506 |         intro ij
507 |         rw [setIntegral_const, measureReal_prod_prod]
508 |         simp only [c, F, map_mul, Complex.conj_ofReal,
509 |           Algebra.smul_def, Complex.coe_algebraMap]
510 |         ring
511 |       have hS_part : (∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) * K (x i) (x j)) =
512 |           ∑ (ij : Fin n × Fin n),
513 |           ∫ z in disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2, F (x ij.1, x ij.2) ∂(μ.prod μ) := by
514 |         rw [← Finset.sum_product', Finset.univ_product_univ]
515 |         exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun ij _ => h_term ij)
516 |       have hIS : I - ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) * K (x i) (x j) =
517 |           ∑ (ij : Fin n × Fin n),
518 |           ∫ z in disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2,
519 |             (F z - F (x ij.1, x ij.2)) ∂(μ.prod μ) := by
520 |         rw [hI_part, hS_part, sub_eq_add_neg, ← Finset.sum_neg_distrib,
521 |           ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
522 |         apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
523 |         intro ij _
524 |         rw [← sub_eq_add_neg, ← integral_sub (hInt' ij) ((integrable_const _).integrableOn)]
525 |       have hUC : ∀ (ij : Fin n × Fin n),
526 |           ∀ z ∈ disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2,
527 |           ‖F z - F (x ij.1, x ij.2)‖ ≤ ε := by
528 |         intro ij z hz
529 |         have ha : z.1 ∈ disjointed B ij.1 := hz.1
530 |         have hb : z.2 ∈ disjointed B ij.2 := hz.2
531 |         have ha_sub : disjointed B ij.1 ⊆ B ij.1 := disjointed_subset B ij.1
532 |         have hb_sub : disjointed B ij.2 ⊆ B ij.2 := disjointed_subset B ij.2
533 |         have ha_dist : dist z.1 (x ij.1) < δ / 2 := ha_sub ha
534 |         have hb_dist : dist z.2 (x ij.2) < δ / 2 := hb_sub hb
535 |         have hdist : dist z (x ij.1, x ij.2) < δ := by
536 |           rw [Prod.dist_eq]
537 |           exact (max_lt ha_dist hb_dist).trans (by linarith [δpos])
538 |         have hnorm : ‖F z - F (x ij.1, x ij.2)‖ < ε := by
539 |           have := hδ hdist
540 |           rwa [dist_eq_norm] at this
541 |         exact le_of_lt hnorm
542 |       have hSumMeas : ∑ (ij : Fin n × Fin n),
543 |           (μ.prod μ).real (disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2) = 1 := by
544 |         rw [← measureReal_iUnion_fintype hDisj hMeas', ← hCover]
545 |         simp [measureReal_def]
546 |       rw [hIS]
547 |       calc ‖∑ (ij : Fin n × Fin n),
548 |           ∫ z in disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2,
549 |             (F z - F (x ij.1, x ij.2)) ∂(μ.prod μ)‖
550 |           ≤ ∑ (ij : Fin n × Fin n),
551 |               ‖∫ z in disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2,
552 |                   (F z - F (x ij.1, x ij.2)) ∂(μ.prod μ)‖ :=
553 |             norm_sum_le _ _
554 |         _ ≤ ∑ (ij : Fin n × Fin n),
555 |               ε * (μ.prod μ).real (disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2) := by
556 |             apply Finset.sum_le_sum
557 |             intro ij _
558 |             exact norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const (by finiteness) (hUC ij)
559 |         _ = ε * ∑ (ij : Fin n × Fin n),
560 |               (μ.prod μ).real (disjointed B ij.1 ×ˢ disjointed B ij.2) := by
561 |             rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
562 |         _ = ε * 1 := by rw [hSumMeas]

565 |   refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
